chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wassa' from Abdullah ibn Sinan said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, chose something from every thing. He chose the she-camel from the camels, and from the sheep, the ewe.

key_terms.الضَّائِنَةَ: The ewe (specifically a young female sheep)

ai.seo_question: What did Allah choose from the camels and sheep according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) illustrates the divine principle of *ikhtiyar* (selection) by citing the she-camel and the ewe as superior exemplars within their respective categories. This narration, found in *Al-Kafi*, reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that Allah’s choice often pertains to utility, gentleness, and specific virtues inherent in the selected creature, serving as a metaphor for spiritual and physical excellence.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, form Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Chose something from everything. He<sup>azwj</sup> Chose the she-camel from the camels, and from the sheep, the ewe’.
en.sarwar: 11. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has chosen something from everything and from camels, He has chosen she-camels and from sheep He has chosen ewes.’”
